messages.text: I’ll use $kk:brainstorm to weigh whether caching across runs is worth pursuing, keeping manual invocation and local processing fixed.

Cross-run caching could save most of the 20-second wait when a report’s inputs haven’t changed. The payoff depends on how often that happens; “public data” remains an assumption to verify before choosing disk storage. Manual invocation and local processing stay settled.

How often do users rerun the same report with unchanged inputs across separate CLI runs?

That correction rules out cross-run caching of report data. Any retained copy would violate the approved rule, including encrypted copies. The earlier disk-cache premise no longer holds.

Manual invocation and local-only processing remain settled. My recommendation is to **discard cross-run report caching** under the current constraint.

The next useful investigation is where the 20 seconds goes. Faster computation or reuse within a single process might help; their value depends on the bottleneck and whether calculations repeat during one invocation. Those remain open, but neither blocks closing the cross-run caching decision.

You’ve decided to **drop cross-run caching**: reports contain confidential customer data, and no report data may persist after process exit, even encrypted.

Generation remains manually invoked and entirely local. Each invocation needs one report, and the current 20-second wait is tolerable.

Next, investigate where computation time goes before deciding whether to optimize. A useful improvement is not yet established; optimization choices and implementation details can wait for that evidence.
